title: The Evidence That Didn't Disappear
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Agasa, Haibara, Ayumi, Mitsuhiko, Genta) omitted by convention. case_type: theft (dognapping / jewel theft), no human victim -- the target is a diamond hidden in a dog's collar, and the dog Doyle is briefly endangered/hidden as a side effect. `label.murderer_id` is kept as the field name for schema consistency but here names the thief, Yoshio Tsunashima; the old wiki-derived case file at cases/ also named Tsunashima (s1) as culprit, so no correction was needed there. However the old file mismodeled the case heavily: it had no clock-diamond object, folded the stereo/tape-recorder trick and the theft into one generic event, omitted the frame-up of Shino Hasuki via her planted shoes, omitted Aki Tosabayashi's red-herring grudge motive, omitted the working dogs Arthur and Christie (who are structurally central -- Arthur's scent tracking locates the speaker cache and both dogs physically intercept Tsunashima's escape), and omitted Tsunashima's stated motive (needing money to stop starving/poisoning unsellable abandoned dogs at his own kennel). Dogs (Arthur, Christie, Doyle) are modeled as `object` nodes with role `instrument`/`evidence` since the schema's `person` type is reserved for humans, but they carry `attrs` describing their plot-relevant behavior. Two-part episode; all present-day action is treated as one continuous day (no `years_before_present` needed) except explicitly-marked prior visits, tagged `temporal_frame: backstory`.

clues.desc: Cushion-count discrepancy: only two blue cushions were accounted for in the house earlier, but after Arthur's search a third blue cushion turns up (the one used as bait, later returned) -- comparing the earlier count against the later count exposes that a cushion had been moved and reused rather than simply overlooked.

Material match: the glittering, cotton-like fiber found stuck to the returned blue cushion is the same heat-resistant glass wool found half-burned in the backyard incinerator -- tying the cushion's hiding place (the gutted speaker) to the incinerator burning, and both back to the same culprit.

Clock drift comparison: the Japanese-room clock was accurate at noon, 3 minutes slow at 3pm, and 5 minutes slow at 5pm -- a steady minute-per-hour drift only explained by a hidden weight dragging on the pendulum, and only the person collecting that clock (Tsunashima) stood to benefit from hiding something inside it.

edges.detail: earlier visit(s) during which Tsunashima learned Doyle's noon-snack habit from Kanou's parents and recorded the clock's chime
gutted the sound-absorbing glass wool from the right speaker in advance and left the back panel prepared, creating a concealed cavity
recorded the Japanese-room noon chime with the borrowed tape recorder on an earlier visit
while everyone was gathered at the entrance for Hasuki's arrival, set the recorded chime tape and Doyle's scented cushion (with sleeping-pill cheese) inside the gutted speaker

edges.method: played the pre-recorded chime from the living-room stereo instead of the real clock, drawing Doyle to his own scented cushion and drugged cheese hidden in the speaker

edges.detail: Doyle is discovered missing from the Japanese room; the group splits up to search the house
Tsunashima pretends to search behind the stereo, in fact removing Doyle's collar while the dog sleeps inside the speaker
removes the diamond from Doyle's collar while the dog is asleep, drugged, in the speaker cavity
wedges the diamond behind the pendulum of the grandfather clock he is due to collect the next day
returns Doyle's scented cushion to the Japanese room, closes the speaker's back panel, and resets the grandfather clock to the correct time
plants Hasuki's shoes near the incinerator and leaves the back door unlocked, to make it look like an outside intruder kidnapped Doyle and fled that way
points to the shoes found by the incinerator as proof Hasuki must have trained Christie to fetch and return them, faking her own alibi
Arthur scent-tracks Doyle to the living room and the speaker cavity during the staged re-enactment
Kanou, prompted by Conan, lays out and confirms the reconstructed method behind Doyle's disappearance
bolts after being named as the culprit

edges.motive_type: grudge_over_dog_show_loss (red herring, no actual crime committed)
